title: StrataDocument
description: A Strata music analysis document (.strata file). The file format is the core invention — everything else is downstream of getting this schema right.

strataVersion.description: Version of the Strata app that created this file (semver string). Used for diagnosing compatibility issues.

fileFormatVersion.description: Version of this file format (2 at present). It goes up when a change means older files must be upgraded to be read correctly; the app upgrades an older file when it opens it (src/lib/migrations.ts).

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of file creation. Set once on first save; never updated.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last save. Updated on every save.

title.description: Display title of the track or recording.

artist.description: Performer or artist name(s). Array to support multiple artists cleanly — e.g. ['The Chainsmokers', 'Halsey']. Single-artist tracks use a one-element array. May be empty while an analysis is in progress: the field is always present, the names are not required.

context.description: Nature of the artifact. 'recording' = studio recording; 'performance' = live performance of a composed work. Null if unspecified. 'performance' shows the composer field in the app.

duration.description: Track duration in seconds (float). Stored explicitly so span timestamps can be validated against the total length.

composer.description: Composer of the work. Shown in the app when context = 'performance'.

work.description: Composition identifier — e.g. 'Piano Sonata Op. 13'. Lets different performances of the same work be compared across files.

notes.description: Document-level free text: methodological notes, analytical caveats, a summary of findings. Distinct from commentary (a written-analysis layer), which is tied to the timeline.

bpm.description: Starting tempo in beats per minute: what a new beatGrid segment starts from, and what quick setup uses before there is a grid. Once the track has a grid, its segments hold the tempo, and this value is not kept in step with them. Null if not set.

beatGrid.description: Bars and beats, laid down by the analyst in segments. Each segment starts on a downbeat and keeps one tempo and meter; the time between segments has no grid (a freeform passage). Beats are computed from the segments, never stored. Omit when the analysis has no grid.

project.description: Corpus or collection tag, for grouping related files in whatever tool gathers them — e.g. 'anthemics-edm-corpus'. The app stores it and does nothing else with it.

layers.description: The analytical layers, each a widget instance. Drawing order comes from each layer's displayOrder, not from its place in this list.

pointMarkers.description: Single-moment events in the recording (a medial caesura, an energy peak, a flagged observation). Stored once for the document, so they show across all layers.

showCadenceCaptions.description: Whether cadence-related point marker detail (type abbreviation, harmonic context) renders on the diagram. Point markers aren't layer-owned, so this is document-level rather than per-layer. Omit/absent = true (shown).

DerivativeReference.description: When this track is derived from another (remix, cover, re-recording, etc.), this field records the relationship. Null for original recordings. The app keeps it but has no control to set it yet.

sourceTrack.description: Filename of the analysis file representing the source track — e.g. 'heroes-original.strata'.

relationship.description: Nature of the derivative relationship. Suggested values: 'remix', 'cover', 'rerecording', 'arrangement'. Free text is accepted — the suggested list is not exhaustive.

GridSegment.description: One stretch of the beat grid. Runs from its first downbeat until its own end, the next segment, or the end of the track, whichever comes first.

start.description: Recording time of the segment's first downbeat, seconds.

end.description: Where the grid stops and a free stretch begins. Null or absent: it runs to the next segment or the end of the track.

beatsPerBar.description: Beats in a bar: the time signature's numerator.

beatUnit.description: The note value of a beat (the time signature's denominator). Display only. Omit for 4.

firstBar.description: Bar number at the segment's start. Null or absent: continue counting from the previous segment.

TimeSignature.description: Starting meter: what a new beatGrid segment starts from, in the same way as bpm. Once the track has a grid, its segments hold the meter. Null if not set.

numerator.description: Number of beats per measure — e.g. 4 in common time.

denominator.description: Note value that receives one beat, expressed as a power of 2 — e.g. 4 = quarter note.

HomeKey.description: The document's tonic and mode. Lets Span.keyArea and PointMarker.harmonicContext store a Roman-numeral RELATIONSHIP (e.g. 'vi', 'V/V') rather than an absolute key name, since the relationship is what's corpus-queryable across pieces in different keys. Null if not set.

tonic.description: Free text — e.g. 'A', 'F#', 'Bb'. Spelling (sharp vs. flat) is the analyst's call, not enum-constrained.

mode.description: A VocabTerm id, resolved against vocabulary.modes plus the built-in modes list shipped in code (major, minor, and the church modes). Project-level custom modes (e.g. Renaissance 8-mode/12-mode systems) go in vocabulary.modes.

SourceReference.description: Reference to the audio or video source. Stored as an object so that sourceOffset is unambiguously coupled to the source it describes.

url.description: Full YouTube video URL. Required when type = 'youtube'.

filename.description: Audio filename only (no folder path). Required when type = 'local'. Not shareable — the file must be present on the viewer's machine.

sourceOffset.description: Offset in seconds between the source file's start and the recording's true start. player_time = recording_time + sourceOffset. All span timestamps are stored in recording time. Updating the offset corrects all seek behavior without touching span data.

Vocabulary.description: Vocabulary terms defined in this file, beyond the built-in libraries that ship with the app: custom span types (including form letters), point marker types and modes.

modes.description: Project-level custom modes (e.g. Renaissance 8-mode/12-mode systems, or any terminology beyond the built-in major/minor/church-mode starter list shipped in code).

id.description: Stable identifier. Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens. Used as the corpus-queryable type value in spans and point markers. Changing this ID breaks corpus queries against existing files.

label.description: Human-readable display name shown in the type picker.

description.description: Explanation shown as a tooltip when the analyst is choosing a type.

color.description: Optional default colour for items of this type. The app keeps it but does not draw with it yet.

kind.description: Whether this term applies to spans, point markers, or modes. Required for vocabulary pack import to route terms correctly.

source.description: Pack provenance string, e.g. 'My Pack v1.0.0'. Set on import; absent for built-ins and project-local terms.

broader.description: Ids of more general terms this one counts as in a query (SKOS 'broader'): a 'caplin-transition' with broader ['transition'] is found by a search for all transitions. Built-in or custom ids.

LayerRenderingConfig.description: Where this layer's span text sits. All spans in the layer share these settings; there are no per-span overrides. The app draws them when a file sets them, but has no control to set them yet. Defaults: label above/center, annotation inside/left.

labelPosition.description: Where span labels sit: 'above' the bracket (default) or 'inside' it.

labelJustification.description: Horizontal alignment of label text. Default: 'center'.

annotationPosition.description: Where annotation text sits: 'inside' the bracket (default) or 'above' it.

annotationJustification.description: Horizontal alignment of annotation text. Default: 'left'.

Layer.description: One analytical layer. Every layer carries the same envelope fields; the shape of data depends on its type.

type.description: Widget type: 'form-diagram' (spans on a timeline) or 'written-analysis' (commentary anchored to spans or times). Possible future types: 'energy-contour', 'instrumentation'. A reader that meets a type it doesn't know should keep the layer unchanged.

label.description: Short human-readable layer name. Displayed in the layer panel.

description.description: Optional longer description of this layer's analytical purpose or framework — e.g. 'Hepokoski/Darcy exposition analysis' or 'Phrase-level hypermeter, 4-bar units'. Distinct from label.

visibility.description: Whether the layer is shown. Hidden layers are left out of exports.

locked.description: When true, the layer cannot be edited — only viewed and exported.

fillColorDefault.description: Fill for spans in this layer that have no fillColor of their own: a hex colour, or 'none' for no fill.

strokeColorDefault.description: Outline for spans in this layer that have no strokeColor of their own: a hex colour, or 'none' for no outline.

displayOrder.description: Drawing order. Lower numbers are drawn first, at the bottom of the stack. Gaps are allowed.

position.description: Reserved: where this layer sits relative to the timeline ruler. The app always draws layers above the ruler and has no control for this yet.

rendering.description: Text rendering defaults for spans in this layer. Omit to use system defaults (label above/center, annotation inside/left).

spanShape.description: How this layer's spans are drawn. Absent or 'bracket' = brackets. 'bar' draws thin flat bars instead — meant for key-area layers (Span.keyArea captions), though any layer may use it. Purely visual; the same span data and editing apply either way.

fillGaps.description: Editing behaviour: whether a boundary placed in an empty stretch of this layer fills it on both sides (true, the default when absent) or starts a span there and leaves the stretch before it empty (false).

library.description: The vocabulary library this layer draws its types from (an id such as 'pop-rock' or 'caplin', or 'letters'). The Type picker and Quick pick lead with it. A working preference for the editor; it does not restrict which types the layer may use. Absent = guessed from the types already in the layer.

fontScale.description: Text size for this layer's labels and annotations: sm (label 9.5px / annotation 8.5px), md (11 / 9), lg (13 / 11). Absent = md. Uniform within a layer; no per-span font size. Purely visual.

data.description: Widget-specific data payload. Shape is determined by the type field.

WrittenAnalysisData.description: Data payload for a written-analysis layer: prose anchored to the timeline. Hierarchy lives in the writing and its links, not in nested data.

AnalysisBlock.description: One piece of commentary. It surfaces while its anchor plays.

anchor.description: What the commentary is about: a span (by its id, which never changes) or a time range in recording seconds. Deleting a span converts its commentary to a time range, so the text is never lost.

text.description: The commentary, in Markdown: paragraphs, **bold**, *italic*, code, headings, lists, quotes and web links. [[slug]] (or [[slug|shown text]]) links to the span or point marker with that slug. Raw HTML is shown as typed, never rendered; images are dropped.

FormDiagramData.description: Data payload for a form-diagram layer.

Span.description: A time range representing a formal section: the core analytical record.

id.description: Auto-generated UUID. Never changes and is never shown to the analyst. Used for references between spans, commentary and merges.

label.description: Display name set by the analyst. Null for unlabelled spans (e.g. bar-level hypermeter spans, where the type carries the meaning). An empty string is valid for a newly placed span awaiting a label.

shortLabel.description: Optional abbreviation of label, written by the analyst (e.g. 'Verse 1' -> 'V1'). Shown above the shape in place of the full label when that doesn't fit at the current zoom; never itself truncated. If neither fits, nothing is drawn there, and the editor shows the label when the span is hovered or selected.

slug.description: Generated from the label — e.g. 'Drop 1' → 'drop-1'. The readable reference name used by commentary links ([[drop-1]]) and embeds. Unique across the document, in one namespace with point-marker slugs: a repeat gets a suffix (verse, verse-2, …) in time order. Frozen once saved, so relabelling keeps it. Null if there is no label.

startTime.description: Start of span in recording time, seconds (float).

endTime.description: End of span in recording time, seconds (float). Must exceed startTime.

type.description: Vocabulary term id: the queryable classification of this section, from the built-in libraries or vocabulary.spanTypes. Separate from label by design.

fillColor.description: This span's fill: a hex colour, or 'none' for no fill. Null = the layer's fillColorDefault.

strokeColor.description: This span's outline: a hex colour, or 'none' for no outline. Null = the layer's strokeColorDefault.

annotation.description: Text drawn on the span alongside the label, for observations that belong on the diagram — e.g. 'filter sweep → snare roll', '+Kick'. Also shown with the span in the commentary panel. Distinct from notes (never shown on the diagram) and from label (the section name).

notes.description: The analyst's working note. Shown only in the Inspector: not drawn on the diagram and not shown in the reading view, embeds or exports.

lyrics.description: Lyric text sung during this span. Shown with the span in the commentary panel, not on the diagram. Queryable.

keyArea.description: Free text, conventionally a Roman numeral relative to StrataDocument.homeKey (e.g. 'vi', 'V/V'); accidentals are stored as ♭/♯. Queryable independently of label and type. Drawn as a caption across the span — most naturally on a layer with spanShape = 'bar', but any span may carry it.

startBoundaryType.description: Character of the formal transition at the start of this span. 'definite' = a clean cut; 'gradual' = a processual transition (a buildup that gradually becomes the section); 'elided' = this span's start is formally simultaneous with the end of the one before. Null or omit for 'definite'. An analytical claim; how the end is drawn is startCap.

endBoundaryType.description: Character of the formal transition at the end of this span; same values as startBoundaryType. Elision is marked per side: this span can claim it whether or not the next span does. Spans in a layer never overlap in the data; an elided end is drawn reaching past the boundary.

parentId.description: Id of the span this one belongs to, on another layer — e.g. this phrase belongs to that section. Set by Group (the grouped spans' parent is the new span) and Copy to layer (of a span and its copy, the one on the higher layer is the parent). In the editor, a parent and its children move their shared boundaries together, and unlinking clears this field. Nothing enforces that a child lies inside its parent. Null if this span has no parent.

mergedFrom.description: Ids of the spans a merge made this one from, in time order: a record of origin, used when the merge carries their commentary over. At least two when present. Null for spans not produced by a merge.

startCap.description: How the start of the bracket is drawn — the analyst's drawing choice, separate from startBoundaryType (the analytical claim). 'rounded' = vertical tail with a rounded corner; 'square' = sharp corner; 'angled' = diagonal tail; 'open' = no tail; 'elision' = a tail reaching past the boundary so it overlaps the neighbour. Absent = follows startBoundaryType ('elided' → 'elision', otherwise 'rounded').

endCap.description: How the end of the bracket is drawn. Same values as startCap; absent = follows endBoundaryType.

lineStyle.description: Stroke of the whole bracket, the analyst's drawing choice. Solid and dashed are never mixed within one shape. Absent = 'solid'.

fillPattern.description: A faint texture drawn over the fill, in a darker shade of the fill colour: diagonal hatching, cross-hatching, dots or horizontal lines. A second cue besides colour (for colour-blind readers, or print in grey). Visual only; carries no analytical claim. Absent = no pattern.

endOnTop.description: Drawing order at this span's end boundary, where an elision makes its bracket overlap the next span's: true = this span draws on top. Absent or false = the next span draws on top. Visual only; carries no analytical claim.

PointMarker.description: A single-moment analytical event. Belongs to the document, not to a layer.

slug.description: Reference name for commentary links ([[slug]]), derived from the label. Shares one namespace with Span.slug, so it is unique across the document. Frozen once saved: relabelling the marker keeps it. Null when the marker has no label.

type.description: Vocabulary term id, from the built-in lists or vocabulary.pointMarkerTypes. Queryable.

flagged.description: 'Come back to this.' A bookmark for moments the analyst wants to revisit. Omit for false.

absent.description: 'This expected event does not occur here.' Significant in Hepokoski/Darcy and similar frameworks, where a missing event has formal consequences. Set with the Absent switch in the marker's panel; the caption is then drawn struck through. Omit for false.

harmonicContext.description: Free text, conventionally a Roman numeral relative to StrataDocument.homeKey (e.g. 'V' for a half cadence in the dominant). Captioned with the type as 'V:PAC', or alone without one, but stored separately. Queryable independently of type.

kind.description: A preset for the editor: picks which fields the marker's panel leads with. Never restricts what a marker can carry; every field stays reachable. Absent behaves like 'other'.
